subject: Priority ask: tag-based routing + warm-pool for FinBridge scaled scoring
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Priority ask: tag-based routing + warm-pool for FinBridge scaled scoring

Team —

Quick context: FinBridge (Sarah Cho/Tom Reilly) is moving to final legal review this week but the execs pushed back on our latency guardrails for their scheduled scoring jobs. Their contract ask is specific: for scoring jobs tagged as "high-risk" they need p95 inference latency <= 200ms during scheduled batch windows and predictable failover that won’t blow past cost bands.

Current platform routes by model + tenant and offers warm pools at the model level. The gap: they want routing by an incoming request tag (risk_level) so requests marked high-risk route to a pinned warm pool with pre-populated KV context. That combined behavior (tag-based routing + tag-keyed warm-pool prefetch) is what they require to accept SLA language.

Attached: mutual action plan + latest SOW draft (highlighted).

Asks:
- Can Product/Eng review feasibility and give a prioritized estimate for a canary (limited tenant + tag) that we can ship as a contractual attachment?
- If feasible, can we target a canary readiness date by 2028-07-06? Customer is explicit about timeline.
- Acceptance criteria from Product: what telemetry do you need from FinBridge (trace samples / token distributions / scheduled window sizes)?

This is a high-probability close (deal id FB-2028-Q3-001). Sales is prepared to offer a 3-month credits buffer and a short SLA addendum to buy runway if needed, but we need a product-level commitment to move legal.

Appreciate a quick triage — tagging Marissa to help with the mutual-action plan and Neha/Jonas for product/eng triage.

— Jasmine
Jasmine Liu | Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1-415-555-0172
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Jun 2028 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Priority ask: tag-based routing + warm-pool for FinBridge scaled scoring

Thanks for the clear note and attachments, Jasmine.

A few clarifying questions before I commit a roadmap slot:
1) Traffic shape: during their scheduled windows what’s the baseline QPS and what’s the peak burst (short-term spike)?
2) Tag semantics: is "high-risk" a binary flag or an ordinal scale (low/med/high)? Do they expect dynamic changes within a window?
3) Failure mode: if the pinned warm pool is exhausted, are they OK with automatic fallback to a lower-tier model variant (soft-SLA), or do they require hard guarantees with capacity reservations?
4) Acceptance criteria: please confirm concrete SLOs (p95 target, error budget) and whether FinBridge will provide sample traces and synthetic job traces for validation.

Technical suggestion: we can probably prototype a lightweight router extension that supports an extra request header (x-rd-risk-tag) mapped to a routing group. Warm-pool prefetch keyed by tenant+tag will require changes in our cache-seeding path and a small bookkeeping layer to track warm-pool entries per (tenant,tag). If customer is willing to accept a two-phase commitment (phase 1: per-tenant warm pools + manual pre-seed; phase 2: tag-keyed routing + automation), we can shorten timeline for an initial canary.

I’ll coordinate with Eng (Jonas) for an estimate. Jonas — can you flag capacity or infra blockers? Marissa — can you confirm that FinBridge will provide the traces and sign the MAP if we can commit a canary date?

-Neha
Neha Kapoor | Director, Product Management — Serving Platform
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 16 Jun 2028 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Priority ask: tag-based routing + warm-pool for FinBridge scaled scoring

Looping in technical perspective. TL;DR: feasible with staged delivery; we can reuse routing table plumbing but warm-pool semantics need a small extension and test coverage.

Detailed notes:
- Router: adding a request-level routing key (x-rd-risk-tag) is straightforward; that maps to an existing routing group abstraction. Estimated effort: 2 dev-days to add header mapping + tests.
- Warm-pool prefetch: current warm-pool is model scoped. To support tenant+tag pre-seed we need: (a) prefetch orchestration changes (scheduler + backend seed API), (b) bookkeeping for per-(tenant,tag) entries to avoid over-allocating GPUs, (c) new metrics (warm_pool_fill_rate, per_tag_misses). Estimated effort: 8-12 dev-days + 3 QA-days.
- Rollout: require a canary path (config flag per tenant) and observability hooks (per-tag latency, miss rate). We already have most tracing; will need a short eval job harness from FinBridge to validate p95 under load.
- Tradeoff/mitigation: if timeline is tight we can offer initial delivery with per-tenant warm pools + a manual pre-seed workflow (operator-run pre-seed) — this cuts effort to ~4 dev-days + 2 QA-days. Tag-based routing would then be delivered in sprint 2.

Questions for Sales/Product:
1) Can FinBridge accept the operator-run pre-seed for short-term contract acceptance?
2) What is the target canary scope (one account + X scoring jobs / window)?
3) Are they amenable to starting with a soft SLA (SLA attachment with credits) for first 30 days?

If you want, I can draft a brief tech appendix we can attach to the MAP describing the staged approach and telemetry we’ll deliver.

— Jonas
Jonas Weber | Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sarah Cho <sarah.cho@finbridge.com>, Tom Reilly <tom.reilly@finbridge.com>
Date: Sun, 17 Jun 2028 16:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Priority ask: tag-based routing + warm-pool for FinBridge scaled scoring

Thanks — appreciate the quick triage and the staged approach, both of which help our legal conversation. To answer your questions:

- FinBridge is willing to accept an operator-run pre-seed for up to 30 days if we commit to automated tag-keyed warm pools in the second sprint. They want the canary scope to cover the "high-risk" scheduled batch (one scoring job type; ~12k tokens per job; expected peak burst ~6k QPS over 30s windows). Baseline sustained QPS during windows is ~800 QPS.
- They are open to a soft SLA for the first 30 days if we provide clear telemetry and a remediation play (credits + immediate operator pre-seed).
- FinBridge will share synthetic job traces and a tracing sample (they confirmed in the MAP).

Requested next actions:
1) Neha & Jonas: please confirm a formal estimate (dev days + QA) and whether the operator-run pre-seed approach meets acceptance for a contract clause.
2) Jonas: if agreed, please sketch the minimal telemetry we must expose for legal (per-tag p95, warm_pool_miss_rate, fallback_count).
3) Marissa: can you update the MAP to reflect staged delivery + credit terms and route the updated MAP to procurement?

Customer pressure is real — legal is ready to move if we can attach a tech appendix and a canary commitment (target 2028-07-06 readiness for limited canary). I’m happy to take this to my AMR if you want to escalate.

Attaching an updated MAP with the customer's note highlighted.

— Jasmine
Jasmine Liu | Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
